minutes.headline: Charter committee backed write-in minimum-vote language and heard a ranked choice voting pitch; no votes taken on either.
minutes.summary: The committee reviewed revised town counsel language setting a minimum vote for write-in candidates when no one is on the ballot. Members indicated support without a formal vote. Representatives of a ranked choice voting group presented, and members leaned toward not leading on it. The committee then reviewed charter drafts on the cemetery commission, library trustees, appointments and vacancies, and discussed the schedule for a public hearing.

what_happened.line: Members indicated general support for revised town counsel language setting a minimum vote for write-in candidates; no formal vote was taken.
After a ranked choice voting presentation, the committee took no position and no vote, and members leaned toward holding the idea off.
Members discussed the cost of new voting machines for ranked choice voting and said adoption could wait for the capital plan cycle.
The chair will draft and email a report on the special town meeting vote before the next meeting.
The next meeting was set for November 14, with a public hearing discussed for December 12 and a second hearing in late January.

why_it_matters: Write-in rules and any later ranked choice voting change would alter how local elections are decided, and charter changes would reach voters through a public hearing and a later vote.
Voting machines for ranked choice voting would be a capital cost paid mostly from taxes, and that cost has not yet been planned or voted.
